hard_case: Measured defect (#7947): ripr reported the related test's oracle `assert_eq!(score(2) == 4 && check(2) != Err(E::Bad), true)` as exact_error_variant / strong, taking its kind from the `!=` conjunct. RIPR-SPEC-0231 rule 1 (example 33): that conjunct only excludes a variant and lends no kind; `score(2) == 4` pins, so the oracle is exact_value / strong. The strength and line verdict were already right; the wrong kind showed in the related test's reported oracle. Since #7947's fix ripr reports exact_value / strong.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: score(2) becomes 6, so score(2) == 4 is false
not equivalent: score(2) becomes 0, so score(2) == 4 is false
not equivalent: score(2) is still 4, but score(3) becomes 5 instead of 6
not equivalent: score(2) becomes 1, so score(2) == 4 is false

reasoning: assert_eq!(score(2) == 4 && check(2) != Err(E::Bad), true) pins score(2) through its == conjunct: x * 3, x * 0 and x / 2 fail it, x + 2 passes because it agrees at 2. The != conjunct only excludes E::Bad and lends the oracle no kind, so the oracle is exact_value / strong (RIPR-SPEC-0231 example 33) on an input that leaves one mutant alive.
